body:
MUTATION PROOF for embed-bench candidate 210919f, per the chief's standing request (post-01M15QKHPQMRA2EJTWXJZ7KQ0V: every candidate that adds a check should show the check's test failing when the check is removed). Four mutants, each applied alone to the candidate tree, each reverted after; the tree is back to 210919f with git diff empty and embedBench/test 25/25 green.

M1 - remove the diagnostic-origin guard (report.scala label(), so a diagnostic case could reach Calibrated): FAILS 2 - LabelSuite "a diagnostic case can never be Calibrated, whatever the protocol says" (expected DiagnosticOrigin, got diagnostic) and WogDiagnosticSuite "the report is Diagnostic because of the cases' origin, even under the pinned protocol". This is the load-bearing one: it is the guard that keeps WOG, and anything else without an adjudicated set behind it, out of a calibrated claim.

M2 - remove the protocol-drift guard (protocolChecksum != currentProtocol): FAILS 1 - LabelSuite "protocol drift fails closed to Diagnostic with both checksums" (expected ProtocolDrift, got calibrated). Without it a set frozen under an edited protocol would publish as calibrated.

M3 - accept a frozen file whose bytes do not match the recorded checksum (FrozenSet.verify): FAILS 1 - LabelSuite "FREEZE rule: a changed file fails closed with the recorded and actual checksums" (expected ChecksumMismatch, got Right(FrozenSet)).

M4 - corrupt the pinned protocol checksum constant: FAILS 1 - ProtocolSuite "pinned checksum equals the canonical text of the protocol document at this revision". This is the drift detector proving it actually reads the document rather than comparing a constant to itself, which is the failure mode a pinned-constant test usually has.

Not proven by mutation, and I would rather say so than imply coverage I did not demonstrate: the metric arithmetic (recall@level, MRR, macro CIs) is covered by hand-checkable expected values in MetricsSuite rather than by mutants, and the no-story-text canary asserts absence, so a mutant that ADDS text is the meaningful test there and I have not written it. If you want either before landing, say so and I will add them to the candidate rather than as a follow-up.

Separately, the chief's scoping correction is unwound: the contamination law now lives on its own bead bd-01M15R1K434JHHJWKNGHTYKDP3 with the already-committed 95979cd, rv-01M15QGBFHCSTSWQ87XCZ5BK17 is released, and bd-01M14YJ8FG15S0R1ART7DTM1XZ is back to exactly the approved scope - the single JVM-only embedBench lazy val, candidate 210919f, evidence unchanged (embedBench 25/25, compileAll three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll, scalafmtSbtCheck).
